title: SSO session-prune race caused audit-ingest lag and transient user lockouts
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Summary: On 2026-03-02 at ~04:12 UTC we observed a short SSO outage window (approx 9 minutes) and a subsequent spike in missing entries on the primary audit sink. Symptoms were transient user lockouts for interactive sessions, elevated 401s from the auth proxy, and a 12% gap in audit ingestion for the window 04:00–04:20 UTC. Impact: user-facing lockouts for internal SSO users and incomplete audit trails for compliance-sensitive actions.
timeline:
2026-03-02 03:55 UTC - Routine background session-prune job scheduled.
2026-03-02 04:05 UTC - Audit-ingest consumer group experienced a rebalance while a checkpoint migration was in flight.
2026-03-02 04:12 UTC - Auth proxy began returning 401s as token introspection TTLs were refreshed and pruning removed session records before the sink checkpointed corresponding audit events.
2026-03-02 04:21 UTC - On-call rolled the consumer group and rehydrated checkpoint; auth traffic returned to normal.
2026-03-02 05:00 UTC - Initial incident page closed; follow-up investigation ticket opened (this card).
root_cause: A race between the session-prune workers (which aggressively deleted sessions in Redis and emitted tombstones) and the audit-ingest checkpoint migration. The ingest consumer performed a group rebalance at the same time the prune job removed session metadata; transient ordering meant audit events for recently-terminated sessions were not written to the durable sink before checkpoints advanced. The combination of TTL-based token introspection and eventual-consistency in our session cache allowed the auth proxy to reject tokens until downstream caches refreshed, producing transient lockouts.
mitigation_summary: Immediate mitigations performed: 1) paused scheduled prune jobs and reverted the most recent prune config, 2) restarted the audit-ingest consumer group to reprocess uncommitted partitions, 3) increased TTL and added marker-check logic on the auth proxy to avoid rejecting tokens while checkpoint reconciliation is pending.
action_items: AI-1: Implement transactional write path for audit-ingest using Kafka transactional producer to ensure events and checkpoints are atomically advanced (owner: eng-data-streams; estimate: 8d; due: 2026-03-31)

AI-2: Change session-prune workflow to emit a tombstone+sequence number and wait for explicit sink-ack before removing authoritative session store entry (owner: auth-svc; estimate: 5d; due: 2026-03-24)
AI-3: Add automated synthetic test that runs prune+consumer-rebalance scenario in CI to catch regressions (owner: infra-tests; estimate: 3d; due: 2026-03-17)
AI-4: Create a runbook for audit-ingest anomalies including alert thresholds (ingest-lag > 5m or >1% gaps) and immediate steps to reconcile (owner: oncall; estimate: 2d; due: 2026-03-15)
AI-5: Add end-to-end observability dashboards showing audit event sequence continuity per partition and per-region (owner: telemetry; estimate: 5d; due: 2026-03-22)
AI-6: Coordinate a maintenance window for large pruning jobs and gate them behind a global maintenance lock to prevent concurrent rebalance/migration (owner: platform; estimate: 2d; due: 2026-03-18)
AI-7: Security review for proposed tombstone/sequence approach to ensure no replay or leakage (owner: sec-eng; estimate: 1d; due: 2026-03-12)
AI-8: Backfill utility to reconstruct missing audit events from append-only encrypted blobs for compressed windows (owner: eng-data; estimate: 6d; due: 2026-04-05)
